Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the inherited rollout evidence, and both required visual views. I’ll also follow the fish-control bookshelf protocol before deciding whether a transferable mechanism belongs in the candidate.

The inherited guidance points to a narrow open hypothesis: immediate, joint-state phase modulation, while preserving cadence, mean bend, and opposite-half-cycle authority. Before using it, I’m checking the sampled traces and images to confirm which result is strongest, which failure is most informative, and whether the latest three completed iterations warrant a fresh bookshelf consultation.

The image review confirms the score differences are not wake-creation differences: all compared policies self-propel along the same gently curved route, with a coherent alternating top-down wake and compact oblique 3D structures. The latest phase-energy envelope also preserves that wake while worsening the score, so I’m treating actuator intervention—not propulsion—as the unresolved issue. The bookshelf consultation is now informing whether a different local state-feedback mechanism is justified.

The shelf reinforces a conservative choice here: preserve the observed traveling rhythm and use only a bounded half-cycle asymmetry selected from body-frame state. The evaluated v31 policy already implements that invariant and is the sampled score leader; three inherited attempts to reinterpret or further regulate the same terminal surface all regressed. I’m recording that diagnosis and the falsifiable exploitation hypothesis before replacing the prefilled v20 candidate.

The candidate now exactly matches the evaluated v31 policy, and the durable guidance records why the three inherited follow-ups should not be stacked onto it. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner now; this validation is limited to the policy contract and workspace edits and will not run CFD.

The mandated check-runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported on this account—the same infrastructure failure recorded in inherited runs. I’m applying the runner’s immutable checks directly and will repair any policy or guidance failure before finishing.

The direct guidance check found a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice with the prefill marker, so the checker sees two parents even though both IDs are identical. I’m removing only the duplicate parent-list entry so the mandated materiality check can resolve the actual assigned parent; no experiment setting or evidence is changing.

The guidance and editable-boundary checks pass. Julia is unavailable in this environment, so the runner’s executable smoke probe cannot start; I’m compensating with the deterministic schema guard and an exact byte comparison against the already evaluated v31 capture policy.

All available checks now pass: guidance materiality, solver boundary, parameter schema, public functions, prohibited-input scan, and exact match to the evaluated v31 capture. The only unavailable check is execution under Julia because the binary is absent; no CFD was run.

Produced exactly one candidate: the evaluated v31 course-consensus posterior duty-ratio policy.

- Candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- Reasoning and bookshelf transfer: [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- Reusable evidence-backed lesson: [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:188)

Guidance materiality, solver boundary, schema, prohibited-input, and evaluated-policy byte-match checks pass. The check-runner model and local Julia executable were unavailable; no CFD was run. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent entry from `README.md` that prevented the mandated guidance checker from resolving the parent.
